question: For weekly-sales data, I need an analysis of our sales performance around mid-June for the years 2018, 2019, and 2020. Specifically, calculate the percentage change in sales between the four weeks leading up to June 15 and the four weeks following June 15 for each year.
sql:
WITH reference AS (
  SELECT calendar_year, 
         MAX(week_number) as june15_week
  FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
  WHERE calendar_year IN (2018, 2019, 2020)
    AND (
      (calendar_year = 2018 AND week_date >= '2018-06-11' AND week_date < '2018-06-18')
      OR (calendar_year = 2019 AND week_date >= '2019-06-10' AND week_date < '2019-06-17')
      OR (calendar_year = 2020 AND week_date >= '2020-06-15' AND week_date < '2020-06-22')
    )
  GROUP BY calendar_year
),
periods AS (
  SELECT c.calendar_year, c.sales,
         CASE 
           WHEN c.week_number < r.june15_week THEN 'before'
           WHEN c.week_number > r.june15_week THEN 'after'
           ELSE 'reference'
         END as period
  FROM cleaned_weekly_sales c
  JOIN reference r ON c.calendar_year = r.calendar_year
  WHERE c.calendar_year IN (2018, 2019, 2020)
    AND c.week_number BETWEEN (r.june15_week - 4) AND (r.june15_week + 4)
    AND c.week_number != r.june15_week
),
totals AS (
  SELECT calendar_year,
         SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) as total_before,
         SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'after' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) as total_after
  FROM periods
  GROUP BY calendar_year
)
SELECT calendar_year,
       ROUND(1.0 * (total_after - total_before) / total_before * 100, 2) as pct_change
FROM totals
ORDER BY calendar_year
